# The taxonomy {#taxonomy-overview}

The Kailash catalogue is organised into **four layers**, and within
each layer into numbered categories. The catalogue of record is the
tool manifest — a single source of truth that drives packaging, the
menu, the CLI, and (coming to this site) the per-tool reference pages.
Counts below are indicative; the manifest is regenerated per release.

| Layer | Focus | Example categories |
|---|---|---|
| CLASSIC (c-01…c-10) | established security disciplines | information gathering, web assessment, forensics, reverse engineering |
| ATTACK (a-01…a-08) | AI-specific offensive work | AI recon, prompt injection & jailbreaks, model supply chain, data poisoning |
| DEFENCE (d-01…d-07) | evaluation, assurance, governance | runtime defence, detection & observability, evals & benchmarks, provenance & signing |
| OPS (o-01…o-07) | engineering operations | MLOps, compute & serving, vector stores, local inference, agent operability |

Every tool lands in the manifest exactly once, with one primary
category and optional secondary cross-references where dual-use is
real. Categories map to desktop menu sections and to the CLI's
listing — the taxonomy is one vocabulary across all surfaces.
